51845-wolfbane.title: Wolfbane
51845-wolfbane.creator: Unknown
51845-wolfbane.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. This was, he counted, the forty-first day on which he and all of Wheeling had donned the appropriate Sun Re-creation clothing. It was the forty-first day on which the Sun--no longer white, no longer blazing yellow, no longer even bright red--had risen and displayed a color that was darker maroon and always darker.

arxiv-2007-02876.title: A Mathematical Theory of Attention Mila & Université de Montréal, aristide.baratin@umontreal.ca Microsoft Research Montreal, retachet@microsoft.com
arxiv-2007-02876.creator: James Vuckovic
arxiv-2007-02876.description: Abstract Attention is a powerful component of modern neural networks across a wide variety of domains. However, despite its ubiquity in machine learning, there is a gap in our understanding of attention from a theoretical point of view. We propose a framework to fill this gap by building a mathematically equivalent model of attention using measure theory.

arxiv-2106-12855.title: Investigating the structure of gluon fluctuations in the proton with incoherent diffraction at HERA
arxiv-2106-12855.creator: Arjun Kumar, Tobias Toll
arxiv-2106-12855.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Arjun Kumar, Tobias Toll. Impact parameter dependent dipole models are ideal tools for investigating the spatial structure of the proton. We investigate the incoherent e ​ p ep cross section in exclusive J / ψ J/\psi photoproduction as measured by HERA, and find that as | t | |t| increases, the models need several levels of substructure of gluon density fluctuations in order to describe the measured data well. In lieu of a perturbative description, we add this substructure by hand.

arxiv-2201-10088.title: Effective minimal model and unconventional spin-singlet pairing in Kagome superconductor CsV 3 Sb 5
arxiv-2201-10088.creator: Xiao-Cheng Bai 1,2 , Wen-Feng Wu 1,2, Han-Yu Wang 1,2 , Ya-Min Quan 1 , Xian-Long Wang 1,2, Zhi Zeng 1,2, Liang-Jian Zou 1,2
arxiv-2201-10088.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xiao-Cheng Bai 1,2 , Wen-Feng Wu 1,2, Han-Yu Wang 1,2 , Ya-Min Quan 1 , Xian-Long Wang 1,2, Zhi Zeng 1,2, Liang-Jian Zou 1,2. Recently synthesized Kagome compounds AV 3 Sb 5 attract great attention due to the unusual coexistence of the topology, charge density wave and superconductivity.

arxiv-2210-10842.title: MMRNet: Improving Reliability for Multimodal Object Detection and Segmentation for Bin Picking via Multimodal Redundancy
arxiv-2210-10842.creator: Yuhao Chen, Hayden Gunraj, E. Zhixuan Zeng, Robbie Meyer, Maximilian Gilles, Alexander Wong
arxiv-2210-10842.description: Abstract Recently, there has been tremendous interest in industry 4.0 infrastructure to address labor shortages in global supply chains. Deploying artificial intelligence-enabled robotic bin picking systems in real world has become particularly important for reducing stress and physical demands of workers while increasing speed and efficiency of warehouses.

arxiv-2303-17433.title: On Consistent Kinetic Mixing and the Higgs Low-Energy Theorems
arxiv-2303-17433.description: Abstract A popular class of extensions of the Standard Model (SM) are models of a new Abelian gauge boson X X , called dark or hidden photon , that kinetically mixes with the SM photon. We revisit the matching procedure of kinetic mixing terms in the electroweak symmetric phase to the ones in the broken phase.

arxiv-2402-10474.title: One-Bit Quantization and Sparsification for Multiclass Linear Classification via Regularized Regression
arxiv-2402-10474.creator: Reza GhaneDepartment of Electrical EngineeringCalifornia Institute of TechnologyPasadena, CA 91125 rghanekh@caltech.edu, Danil AkhtiamovDepartment of Computing and Mathematical SciencesCalifornia Institute of TechnologyPasadena, CA 91125 dakhtiam@caltech.edu Babak HassibiDepartment of Electrical Eng
arxiv-2402-10474.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Reza GhaneDepartment of Electrical EngineeringCalifornia Institute of TechnologyPasadena, CA 91125 rghanekh@caltech.edu, Danil AkhtiamovDepartment of Computing and Mathematical SciencesCalifornia Institute of TechnologyPasadena, CA 91125 dakhtiam@caltech.edu Babak HassibiDepartment of Electrical Eng. We study the use of linear regression for multiclass classification in the over-parametrized regime where some of the training data is mislabeled.

arxiv-2402-17512.title: Latte: Latent Attention for Linear Time Transformers
arxiv-2402-17512.creator: Rares Dolga, Lucas Maystre, Marius Cobzarenco, David Barber
arxiv-2402-17512.description: Abstract The time complexity of the standard attention mechanism in transformers scales quadratically with sequence length. We propose a probabilistic framework for attention, enabling us to derive a novel low-rank linear re-parameterisation of both bidirectional and causal cases, based on defining a latent variable model. Our method can be seamlessly integrated as a drop-in replacement for the standard attention mechanism.

arxiv-2503-22044.title: CIMPool: Scalable Neural Network Acceleration for Compute-In-Memory using Weight Pools
arxiv-2503-22044.creator: Shurui Li, Puneet Gupta
arxiv-2503-22044.description: Abstract Compute-in-memory (CIM) based neural network accelerators offer a promising solution to the Von Neumann bottleneck by computing directly within memory arrays. However, SRAM CIM faces limitations in executing larger models due to its cell size and on-chip memory constraints.

arxiv-2505-13738.title: Power Lines: Scaling Laws for Weight Decay and Batch Size in LLM Pre-training
arxiv-2505-13738.creator: Shane Bergsma, Nolan Dey, Gurpreet Gosal, Gavia Gray, Daria Soboleva, Joel Hestness
arxiv-2505-13738.description: Abstract Efficient LLM pre-training requires well-tuned hyperparameters (HPs), including learning rate η \eta and weight decay λ \lambda . We study scaling laws for HPs: formulas for how to scale HPs as we scale model size N N , dataset size D D , and batch size B B .

arxiv-2508-04528.title: Localization structure of electronic states in the quantum Hall effect
arxiv-2508-04528.creator: Alioune Seye, Marcel Filoche
arxiv-2508-04528.description: Abstract We investigate the localization of electronic states in the Integer Quantum Hall Effect (IQHE) using a magnetic localization landscape (MLL) approach. By studying a continuum Schrödinger model with disordered electrostatic potential, we demonstrate that the MLL, defined via a modified landscape function incorporating magnetic effects, captures key features of quantum state localization.

arxiv-2509-20488.title: Revisiting Formal Methods for Autonomous Robots: A Structured Survey
arxiv-2509-20488.creator: Atef Azaiez, David A. Anisi, Marie Farrell, Matt Luckcuck
arxiv-2509-20488.description: Abstract This paper presents the initial results from our structured literature review on applications of Formal Methods (FM) to Robotic Autonomous Systems (RAS). We describe our structured survey methodology; including database selection and associated search strings, search filters and collaborative review of identified papers.

arxiv-2512-18911.title: The Lifespan of Strong Solutions to the Compressible MHD Equations with Entropy Transport in the Presence of Vacuum
arxiv-2512-18911.creator: Yongteng G U, Xiangdi H UANG a. State Key Laboratory of Mathematical Sciences, Academy of Mathematics and Systems Sciences,Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100190, China
arxiv-2512-18911.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yongteng G U, Xiangdi H UANG a. State Key Laboratory of Mathematical Sciences, Academy of Mathematics and Systems Sciences,Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100190, China. In this paper, we investigate the finite time blow-up of strong solutions to the compressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) system (without magnetic diffusion) coupled with entropy transport, and derive an upper bound for the lifespan of such solutions.

arxiv-2601-21596.title: Lorentz meets Ptolemy
arxiv-2601-21596.creator: Felix Rott, Zhe-Feng Xu, Matteo Zanardini
arxiv-2601-21596.description: Abstract We consider a Lorentzian analogue of the Ptolemy inequality and we prove that in the setting of globally hyperbolic spacetimes it is equivalent to a global timelike sectional curvature bound from above by zero. We investigate the link between the Ptolemy inequality and the hyperbolic inversion and establish some applications and rigidity properties.

britannica-1911-ess-johann-heinrich-van.description: Article 'Ess, Johann Heinrich van' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 9), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. theologian, was born at Warburg, Westphalia, on the 15th of February 1772. He was educated at the Dominican gymnasium of his native town, and in 1790 entered, as a novice, the Benedictine abbey of Marienmünster, in the bishopric of Paderborn. His Benedictine name was Leander.

pmc-10618188.title: Nanopore long-read RNA sequencing reveals functional alternative splicing variants in human vascular smooth muscle cells
pmc-10618188.creator: Hao Wu, Yicheng Lu, Zhenzhen Duan, Jingni Wu, Minghui Lin, Yangjun Wu, Siyang Han, Tongqi Li, Yuqi Fan, Xiaoyuan Hu, Hongyan Xiao, Jiaxuan Feng, Zhiqian Lu, Deping Kong, Shengli Li
pmc-10618188.description: Vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) are the major contributor to vascular repair and remodeling, which showed high level of phenotypic plasticity. Abnormalities in VSMC plasticity can lead to multiple cardiovascular diseases, wherein alternative splicing plays important roles. However, alternative splicing variants in VSMC plasticity are not fully understood.

pmc-11432741.title: Unraveling the Genetic Control of Pigment Accumulation in Physalis Fruits
pmc-11432741.creator: Wennan Zhao, Haiyan Wu, Xiaohan Gao, Huimei Cai, Jiahui Zhang, Chunbo Zhao, Weishu Chen, Hongyu Qiao, Jingying Zhang, Abir U Igamberdiev
pmc-11432741.description: Physalis pubescens and Physalis alkekengi, members of the Physalis genus, are valued for their delicious and medicinal fruits as well as their different ripened fruit colors—golden for P. pubescens and scarlet for P. alkekengi. This study aimed to elucidate the pigment composition and genetic mechanisms during fruit maturation in these species.

pmc-11642348.title: High-Density Lipoprotein Predicts Intrahospital Mortality in Influenza
pmc-11642348.creator: Matthias Wolfgang Heinzl, Markus Freudenthaler, Paul Fellinger, Lisa Kolenchery, Michael Resl, Carmen Klammer, Florian Obendorf, Lukas Schinagl, Thomas Berger, Margot Egger, Benjamin Dieplinger, Martin Clodi
pmc-11642348.description: Background: Although it is known that high-density lipoprotein (HDL) exerts important anti-inflammatory effects and that low HDL plasma concentrations represent a negative prognostic marker in bacterial infections and sepsis, not much is known about possible implications of HDL in acute viral infections such as influenza.

pmc-12634416.title: Epidemiological associations between obesity, metabolism and disease risk: are body mass index and waist-hip ratio all you need?
pmc-12634416.creator: Ville-Petteri Mäkinen, Siyu Zhao, Andrei Ihanus, Tuulia Tynkkynen, Mika Ala-Korpela
pmc-12634416.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/ObjectivesTracking excess adiposity at population scale is essential for managing the obesity pandemic in human populations. New formulas based on weight, height, waist and hip measurements have been suggested as better alternatives to the classic body mass index and waist-hip ratio, but the lack of systematic benchmarking on how these formulas reflect adiposity, metabolic dysfunction and clinical sequelae causes confusion on how to best monitor the health of populations.Subjects/MethodsParticipants from the Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966 were included based on data availability

pmc-12785745.title: Glucose Metabolism and Innate Immune Responses in Influenza Virus Infection: Mechanistic Insights and Clinical Perspectives
pmc-12785745.creator: Kareem Awad, Nancy N. Shahin, Tarek K. Motawi, Maha Abdelhadi, Reham F. Barghash, Ahmed M. Awad, Laura Kakkola, Ilkka Julkunen
pmc-12785745.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This review article discusses glucose metabolic alterations affecting immune cell responses to influenza virus infection. It highlights possible relationships between essential metabolic targets and influenza replication dynamics in immune cells. Thus, kinases as essential regulators of glucose metabolism as well as critical immune mediators during this infection such as interferons, tumor necrosis factor-alpha and transforming growth factor beta have been illustrated.

pmc-13024869.title: Simultaneous Transmission of Discrete-Variable Quantum Key Distribution and Classical Optical Communication in Few-Mode Fiber
pmc-13024869.creator: Qi Zhao, Gang Wang, Li Pei, Jianjun Tang, Yuheng Xie, Zhenhua Li, Yang Liu
pmc-13024869.description: Based on mode crosstalk theory, this paper develops a spontaneous Raman scattering (SpRS) model for the quantum-classical coexistence system using few-mode fiber (FMF) integrated with wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) and spatial-division multiplexing (SDM). Through numerical calculations, the influence degrees of three factors (mode coupling, the number of modes and wavelengths) on SpRS are analyzed.

pmc-13398562.title: Post‐hatching development of the remote‐tactile bill‐tip organ in precocial shorebirds (Scolopacidae)
pmc-13398562.creator: Carla J. du Toit, Anyaise Green, Daniel J. Field
pmc-13398562.description: Several groups of birds that rely on tactile foraging methods to locate prey exhibit specialized bill‐tip organs to sense tactile cues. Most scolopacid shorebirds (sandpipers and kin) employ the sensory capability of remote‐touch during foraging, allowing them to locate buried prey at a distance from their bills by detecting vibrational cues in the substrates they probe in.

pmc-13509449.title: AI-Guided Long Non-Coding RNA Target Discovery for Precision Medicine: Integrating GWAS, Multi-Omics, Experimental Validation, and RNA Therapeutics
pmc-13509449.creator: Mia Yang Ang, Li Chen, Lanni Song, Leonard Lipovich, Siew Woh Choo
pmc-13509449.description: Background/Objectives: Precision medicine requires translation of genetic and molecular variation into clinically actionable therapeutic targets. However, many disease-associated signals identified by genome-wide association studies (GWAS) reside in non-coding regulatory regions, making biological interpretation and therapeutic prioritization difficult. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are regulatory molecules with growing relevance to disease mechanisms, biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and RNA-based therapeutics.

pmc-13640322.title: An advanced genome engineering platform for Komagataella phaffii enabling versatile in vivo DNA assembly and multiplex integration
pmc-13640322.creator: Yujung Choi, Ayoung Kim, Nam Kyu Kang
pmc-13640322.description: BackgroundThe transition toward a sustainable bioeconomy necessitates the development of robust microbial platforms capable of C1 chemical valorization, particularly the conversion of methanol into high-value chemicals. Komagataella phaffii is a premier methylotrophic host for such applications due to its natural methanol utilization pathways and high-density fermentation capabilities.
